{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-load the data to be safe
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Check the revenue values more carefully — perhaps they are stored as '999,999.99'?
# Look for revenue strings that match '999,999.99'
qa_pattern = '999,999.99'
qa_rows = df[df['revenue'] == qa_pattern]

print(f"Number of rows with revenue exactly '999,999.99': {len(qa_rows)}")
print("Sample of such rows:", qa_rows[['order_id', 'revenue', 'status']].head())

# Also check for any other possible QA-like values
# Look for revenue values that are very high and suspicious
# We'll convert to float after cleaning commas, then look for values > 999000
# But first clean the revenue column: remove commas and convert

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
# This will allow us to see all values

# Check for any non-numeric characters in revenue
print("Any non-numeric characters in revenue?", df['revenue'].str.contains(r'[^0-9,.]', regex=True).any())

# Now do clean revenue
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Now look for values > 999000
high_revenue = df[df['revenue_clean'] > 999000]
print(f"Number of orders with revenue > 999,000: {len(high_revenue)}")
print("High revenue values:", high_revenue['revenue_clean'].unique())

# Also check the completed orders
completed_df = df[df['status'] == 'completed']
completed_clean = completed_df[completed_df['revenue_clean'] < 999000]  # Remove suspiciously high ones

# Compute mean revenue for completed orders
mean_revenue = completed_clean['revenue_clean'].mean()
print(f"Mean revenue of completed orders (after cleaning and removing high outliers): {mean_revenue}")

# Output the number of completed orders after filtering
print(f"Number of completed orders after filtering high outliers: {len(completed_clean)}")"}
